## The Resesh agent

- A persistent session can now be kept alive by the Resesh agent instead of tmux. Choose it under "Kept alive by" in the session dialog or in bulk edit.
- The agent passes program output, terminal queries and input through unchanged, where tmux drops or answers most of them.
- After a reconnect it brings back the screen and scrollback with links, command marks and program status, and the command history is not recorded twice.
- Choosing the agent for a session is the consent to upload it to that host. It is a small static binary for x86_64 and ARM64 Linux, placed in `~/.local/share/resesh` and checked before it is used. Nothing needs installing on the server.
- When the agent cannot be used, the session falls back to tmux and a notice in the window says why.
- The agent is built on zmx and libghostty-vt.

## Shared logins

- An identity is a username with a saved password, a registered key, or a password asked once per app run. Set one on a folder and every session inside uses it. Sessions can also choose an identity or keep their own login.
- Settings > Identities & Keys replaces the SSH Keys dialog.
- When an identity's password is rejected, Resesh offers to update it everywhere it is used.
- Import proposes identities for logins that repeat, and its review is now a tab with a folder tree. The SecureCRT import finds more keys and skips RDP sessions.

## Sessions

- Settings gains a Sessions section: one sortable, filterable table of every saved session and local profile. Edit a selection together, move it to a folder, give it an identity, duplicate it or delete it.
- Open several sessions selected in the tree as splits from the context menu.

## Program status on tabs

- Programs can report that they are idle, working, blocked, done or failed (OSC 7501), and the tab shows it as a badge. A percentage drives the tab's progress bar.
- Agent status now shows in persistent sessions kept alive by tmux, for Codex, Claude Code and the shell wrapper adapters. This needs tmux 3.0 or later.
- OpenCode and oh-my-pi are recognized as their own agents, with their own icons.
- Badge symbols are easier to read.
- A connected tab shows the agent icon or badge in place of the connection dot.

## Terminal

- Box drawing, block, braille and Powerline characters are drawn by the terminal itself, so there are no seams between cells at any zoom level.
- Characters missing from your font fall back to system fonts. A bundled Nerd Font draws prompt and status-line icons without a patched font.
- Full-screen programs extend their background into the margin, and programs can set the mouse pointer shape.
- Styled underlines, focus reports and program clipboard copies pass through tmux.
- Terminals in background tabs and minimized windows are no longer drawn, which saves CPU. Their output, notifications and history are unaffected.

## Fixes

- Fixed terminals going blank after a split or after a tab moved between groups.
- Fixed a reattach on tmux 3.4 bringing back only the visible screen.
- Fixed a program's status badge being lost when it reported right after starting.
- The terminal recovers when the graphics device is lost.
- sshfs mounts verify the server's trusted host key.
- A failed save of sessions, keys or settings leaves the existing file unchanged.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
